questions.text_english:
(1) The words probiotics, prebiotics, and postbiotics may sound like variations of the same thing, but what a difference a prefix makes. The first is a category of health-promoting microbes. The latter two groups are types of beneficial molecules. But all three biotics are critical for supporting the community of microscopic organisms that live in the gastrointestinal tract, known as the gut microbiome. With both beneficial and harmful bacteria living in the human body, these diet-related factors the biotics help tip the balance in the positive direction. It is important to understand their differences, as you'll see, because each of these factors serves a distinct purpose, even as they work together.

(2) Despite their importance for the gut microbiome, the health benefits of these 'biotics', which are present in certain foods or result from their metabolism, extend beyond the digestive tract. A growing body of scientific evidence has linked prebiotics, probiotics, and postbiotics, with improvements in metabolic diseases including obesity and cholesterol abnormalities depressive symptoms and poor sleep quality, among many other conditions.

(3) Besides promoting general gut health, consuming food rich in probiotics can improve irritable bowel syndrome and antibiotic-related diarrhea, prevent traveller's diarrhea, produce vitamins and increase nutrient absorption, and decrease the risk of common infections. In fact, when consumed regularly, probiotics have been found to reduce the occurrence of upper respiratory tract infections (like the common cold).

(4) Many different types of beneficial bacteria are considered probiotics. The most common ones include Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium, of which there are dozens of strains. You have to match what it is you're concerned about with the probiotic you should use, says Gregor Reid. Many different types of beneficial bacteria are considered probiotics.

(5) Some foods, such as yogurt, kefir, kimchee, and fermented soybeans and kombucha naturally contain probiotics. But here's where things get complicated: not all fermented foods or yogurts contain probiotics, Reid says. As a consumer, a good starting point is to look for the phrase contains live and active cultures on the label; it's even better if specific strains of bacteria are listed, because then you'll know you're getting the right stuff.

(6) Simply put, prebiotics are sources of food for those beneficial microbes the probiotics. They are typically a form of carbohydrate or fiber that we don't have the enzymes to digest. As a result, they move through the digestive tract to the intestine, where beneficial bacteria (probiotics) can feast on them.

(7) When you consume foods that are rich in probiotics and prebiotics, the microbes in your gut consume the undigestible prebiotic fiber and produce bioactive compounds called postbiotics. They are ultimately the endgame that we want they affect how our gut operates and keeps the good bacteria there and the bad bacteria out.
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions.
questions.solution: Passage-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following statements best describes the author's attitude towards probiotics?

options_english.A: Probiotics, prebiotics and postbiotics are variations of the same thing, with just a difference of a prefix.
options_english.B: All fermented foods or yogurts naturally contain probiotics.
options_english.C: All three biotics are equally important to support microscopic organisms that live in the gut microbiome.
options_english.D: Only probiotics are important as they can improve irritable bowel syndrome and antibiotic-related diarrhea.

sub_questions.solution: The author clearly states in the first paragraph that all three biotics are critical for supporting the community of microscopic organisms that live in the gastrointestinal tract, demonstrating an attitude that values all three equally.

sub_questions.text_english: According to the writer, health benefits of all the biotics' extend beyond the digestive tract. Rationalise your response in about 40 words.

key_points: Link to metabolic diseases like obesity and cholesterol.
Link to depressive symptoms and poor sleep.

sub_questions.solution: The author asserts that the biotics provide benefits outside the digestive tract by linking them to improvements in metabolic diseases, such as obesity and abnormal cholesterol levels, as well as helping to alleviate depressive symptoms and poor sleep quality.

sub_questions.text_english: To get the right probiotic and to match it with your body's requirement, it is important to see the label for _______
sub_questions.solution: Based on paragraph 5, checking the label for specific strains of bacteria is crucial to ensure you are getting the right probiotic for your needs. The complete sentence is: To get the right probiotic and to match it with your body's requirement, it is important to see the label for specific strains of bacteria.

sub_questions.text_english:
The passage includes some words that are opposites of each other. From the sets (A) - (E) below, identify two sets of antonyms.
(A) increase and decrease
(B) probiotic and postbiotic
(C) beneficial and harmful
(D) feast and fermented
(E) consuming and digestive

key_points: A and C

sub_questions.solution: The two sets of antonyms found in the options are (A) increase and decrease, and (C) beneficial and harmful, as they represent direct opposites in meaning.

sub_questions.text_english: The author wants to stress the fact that there is not just one type of beneficial bacteria considered as probiotic, in fact, some probiotics have _______
sub_questions.solution: The author notes that common probiotics like Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium have dozens of strains. The correct sentence is: The author wants to stress the fact that there is not just one type of beneficial bacteria considered as probiotic, in fact, some probiotics have dozens of strains.

sub_questions.text_english: Based on the reading of the passage, examine in about 40 words, the importance of prebiotics for the human gut and how they are related to probiotics.

key_points: Prebiotics serve as food for probiotics.
They are undigestible fibers that beneficial bacteria feast on.

sub_questions.solution: Prebiotics are essential for the gut because they act as a vital food source for probiotics. Made of undigestible fibers and carbohydrates, they travel to the intestine where beneficial bacteria feed on them to produce healthy, bioactive compounds.

sub_questions.text_english: As a consumer, if you want to pick a probiotic product, what is the most important thing to keep in mind? Pick the best answer.

options_english.A: Any fermented product that contains probiotics.
options_english.B: Checking the label for specific strains of bacteria.
options_english.C: All products under probiotics section in a grocery store are safe to pick.
options_english.D: Checking the label which clearly says probiotics is sufficient.

sub_questions.solution: According to paragraph 5, to ensure you are getting the right stuff for your specific needs, checking the label for specific strains of bacteria is the best approach for a consumer.

sub_questions.text_english: Despite their importance for the gut microbiome, the health benefits of these 'biotics', which are present in certain foods or result from their metabolism, extend beyond the digestive tract. As per this statement from the passage, how relevant are the 'biotics' for humans? Pick the best answer.

options_english.A: Their relevance has been proven by scientific evidence.
options_english.B: Not very relevant as more study is needed.
options_english.C: Their relevance cannot be generalised for everyone.
options_english.D: Only probiotics are relevant for humans.

sub_questions.solution: Option A is correct because the passage explicitly states that a growing body of scientific evidence has linked these biotics to widespread health improvements beyond just the digestive tract.

questions.text_english:
(1) After more than two years of halted travel, India's tourism and hospitality industry is now cautiously hopeful. Tourism constituted almost 3% of India's GDP and generated around 100 million jobs in 2019. But the sector was severely hit in India like in other countries in the past two years.

(2) Indians are now travelling with a vengeance 'revenge travel', as the phenomenon is called. And many, experts say, now prefer to travel within the country instead of flying to more expensive destinations abroad. The industry is also benefitting from new trends borne of the pandemic such as micro-holidays and workcations.

(3) According to a survey, 51 percent of Indian travellers believed that international travel remained an important means of expanding their horizons and connecting with other cultures. Over two years, the survey said, Indian travellers are now dreaming about their next international trip and more than 70 percent of Indians are excited about being able to travel internationally.

(4) There has also been an increase in the number of students going abroad to study. The increasing desire to study overseas is credited to the pent-up demand from the pandemic's two-year duration. This has got further pronounced because of growing aspirations and affordability among the middle-class students from Tier II and Tier III cities.

[Table: Foreign travel by Indians for different purposes]

Pilgrimage | 8.8 L | 1-1 L | 4,139 | 4-6 L

questions.instruction_line_english: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions.
questions.image_description: A table showing foreign travel by Indians for different purposes from 2019 to 2022.
questions.solution: Passage-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: We can say that the situation when people were travelling with a vengeance is comparable to people going out to dine in hordes, because _______

fill_values: it reflects pent-up demand being released after a long period of restriction

sub_questions.solution: The phenomenon of 'revenge travel' is akin to people dining out in hordes because both represent a sudden release of intense, pent-up demand immediately following a prolonged period of mandatory restrictions or lockdowns.

sub_questions.text_english: The statement that, 'Tourism constituted almost 3% of India's GDP and generated around 100 million jobs in 2019', is a/an _______ (fact/opinion) because it is a/an _______ (subjective judgement/objective detail).
sub_questions.solution: The correct terms are 'fact' and 'objective detail' because statistical data about GDP and job numbers can be explicitly verified. The sentence is: The statement... is a fact because it is an objective detail.

sub_questions.text_english: Justify the following in about 40 words. After being cooped up inside their houses for more than two years, Indians are now excited about being able to travel internationally.

key_points: People experienced long periods of halted travel.
Survey says over 70 percent are eager to travel and reconnect with cultures.

sub_questions.solution: Indians are highly excited to travel internationally because the pandemic forced a two-year halt on their mobility. With travel resuming, over 70 percent are eager to fulfill pent-up travel desires and reconnect with diverse global cultures.

sub_questions.text_english: Based on the given table, for which 'purpose' did Indian foreign travel increase in 2022 as compared to 2019?

key_points: Education

sub_questions.solution: According to the provided table, travel for the purpose of 'Education' saw an increase from 5.8 Lakhs in 2019 to 6.5 Lakhs in 2022.

sub_questions.text_english: The industry is also benefitting from new trends borne of the pandemic such as micro-holidays and workcations.' Which 'industry' is being talked about here?

key_points: Tourism and hospitality industry

sub_questions.solution: The text refers to the 'tourism and hospitality industry' in India, which is slowly recovering thanks to these new domestic travel trends.

sub_questions.text_english: As per the given table, for which purpose did maximum number of Indians undertake foreign travel in 2019 and in 2022? State any one inference that can be drawn from this.

key_points: Residency for both 2019 and 2022.
Inference: A significant number of Indians seek long-term settlement or permanent opportunities abroad.

sub_questions.solution: The maximum number of Indians traveled abroad for 'Residency' in both 2019 and 2022. This infers a strong, ongoing trend of Indians permanently migrating or settling overseas for better living standards or long-term career prospects.

sub_questions.text_english: Why are students today choosing to go abroad to study? (Answer in about 40 words.)

key_points: Pent-up demand from the pandemic.
Growing aspirations and affordability among middle-class students from Tier II and III cities.

sub_questions.solution: Students are increasingly opting to study abroad due to massive pent-up demand from the two-year pandemic delay. Furthermore, rising affordability and growing aspirations among middle-class families in Tier II and Tier III cities have significantly boosted this trend.

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following is the main takeaway from the study mentioned in the passage?

options_english.A: International travel remains an important means of expanding the horizons and connecting with other cultures.
options_english.B: Though travel, both domestic and international, has picked up, it has yet to reach its previous levels.
options_english.C: Indians are excited about being able to travel internationally.
options_english.D: The study needs to include experts from Tourism Department to offer any recommendations for further research.

sub_questions.solution: The passage primarily highlights the study's finding that despite the long pause, an overwhelming majority (over 70 percent) of Indians are deeply excited to resume international travel, indicating strong 'revenge travel' sentiment.

questions.text_english: Complete any ten of the following twelve tasks, as directed.
questions.solution: Grammar tasks are solved in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blank by using the correct form of the word in the brackets, for the given portion of a letter. Thank you for exceeding company expectations and _______ (inspire) your team with your spectacular work ethic.
sub_questions.solution: The blank requires the gerund form to maintain parallel structure with 'exceeding'. Therefore, 'inspiring' is the correct form. The sentence reads: Thank you for exceeding company expectations and inspiring your team with your spectacular work ethic.

sub_questions.text_english: Read the given sentence from a movie review article. Identify the error and supply the correction in the sentence. The movie doesn't let you rest and is packed with engaged action sequences.
sub_questions.solution: The error lies in the word 'engaged', which incorrectly describes the sequences. The present participle 'engaging' must be used as an adjective to describe action sequences that actively hold attention.

sub_questions.text_english: Akshat and Niharika had a conversation about the felicitation of Akshat's achievements. Report Niharika's question. 'What will you be wearing for tomorrow's function ?'

key_points: Niharika asked Akshat what he would be wearing for the next day's function.

sub_questions.solution: In reported speech, the future tense 'will' changes to 'would', and the time marker 'tomorrow's' shifts to 'the next day's'. The sentence structure changes from interrogative to declarative.

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option, to complete the disclaimer given before a documentary film. The film has been created by taking creative liberties and dramatizing the events _______ (about/for/on) cinematic expressions.
sub_questions.solution: The correct preposition is 'for' because it correctly links the action (dramatizing) to its intended purpose (cinematic expressions). The full sentence is: ...dramatizing the events for cinematic expressions.

sub_questions.text_english: Identify the error and supply the correction for the given sentence from a comment posted by an admirer of a reporter. The report was well document, so no one could claim that it was just one person's opinion.
sub_questions.solution: The error is the use of the base noun/verb 'document' instead of the past participle adjective 'documented'. The passive construction 'was well documented' is grammatically required here.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the given narrative by filling in the blank with the correct option. Now that many employees have shown high productivity working from home, will their bosses hereafter _______ them to take working vacations?
sub_questions.solution: The sentence is an interrogative clause in the future tense using the modal 'will'. Following a modal auxiliary verb, the base form of the main verb 'expect' must be used.

sub_questions.text_english:
Select the correct option to complete the reporting of the dialogue. Teacher: Karan, why were you absent yesterday? 
 Karan: Yesterday I had cold and fever, sir. I couldn't inform you beforehand. 
 The teacher asked Karan _______. Karan replied that he had cold and fever the previous day and added that he couldn't inform the teacher beforehand.

options_english.A: why did he remain absent the previous day
options_english.B: why he had been absent the previous day

sub_questions.solution: In reported speech, the simple past 'were' changes to past perfect 'had been', and 'yesterday' changes to 'the previous day'. The word order shifts from question format to statement format, making option B correct.

sub_questions.text_english: Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the opening line, from a Terms and Conditions document. Though all efforts have been made to ensure the accuracy of the content on this website, the same could not be construed as a statement of law or used for any legal purposes.
sub_questions.solution: The modal 'could' implies past ability, which is inappropriate for a formal forward-looking disclaimer. The prescriptive modal 'should' is proper for stating rules or conditions in official documents.

sub_questions.text_english: Report the following dialogue between a hawker and his customer, by completing the sentence. Hawker: Do you want any tomatoes? Customer: Yes, indeed! Although they are a bit expensive, I like to add tomatoes to my diet. The hawker asked the customer whether she wanted any tomatoes. The customer answered in the affirmative and explained that _______

fill_values: although they were a bit expensive, she liked to add tomatoes to her diet.

sub_questions.solution: When converting to indirect speech, present tense verbs 'are' and 'like' must backshift to 'were' and 'liked'. The pronoun 'I' changes to 'she' to match the customer.

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option to complete the part of the grievance posted by a citizen on a social media platform. Crossing this stretch at any time of the day is a challenge. Even during afternoons, there _______ ice cream vendors on the road with people crowding around their carts.
sub_questions.solution: The passage describes an ongoing, present reality ('is a challenge'). Therefore, the simple present tense 'are' correctly maintains the present tense consistency of the narrative.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the line from a 'Save the Planet' song, by filling in the blank with the correct option. Let's see what we can do / To save the planet for me and you / E is for environment, keep it clean / If we _______ together, we'll make the best team.
sub_questions.solution: This is a first conditional sentence. The 'if' clause must use the simple present tense 'stand' to pair correctly with the future tense 'we'll make' in the main clause.

sub_questions.text_english: Identify the error and supply the correction for the following note in a smart watch's instruction manual. When the watch is connected to the mobile phone, the watch may automatically calibrate and synchronize with the time of the mobile phone.
sub_questions.solution: The error lies in the modal 'may', which indicates mere possibility. In a technical manual describing an automatic system function upon connection, 'will' is correct because it indicates a definite, programmed action.

questions.text_english:
Attempt any one from (a) and (b) given below:

(a) The problem of open manholes and drains in your locality is posing a threat to the lives of people. As a young citizen, who cares about the upkeep of the locality and safety of the residents, write a letter to the editor of a local daily, in about 120 words, expressing your concern at the situation and suggesting measures to resolve the problem and drawing attention of the concerned authorities. You are Sam/Karen of 67, Mist Apartments, Gagan Vihar, Akash Nagar.

OR

(b) As Rohini Monga / Rohan Monga, of 43 Jai Apartments, Neerbagh, you feel that there should be a dedicated space in the community park for the senior citizens of the society, where they can gather. Write a letter to the RWA of your society in about 120 words, suggesting spaces in the park and emphasizing the importance of creating such a space.
questions.instruction_line_english: Write a letter in about 120 words.
questions.solution: Creative Writing tasks are addressed in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: Write a letter to the editor regarding the problem of open manholes.

key_points: Sender address: 67, Mist Apartments, Gagan Vihar, Akash Nagar.
Subject: Threat posed by open manholes and drains.
Body: Describe the danger, especially during nights and monsoons.
Suggest solutions like immediate covering and regular checks.
Conclusion urging civic authorities to take prompt action.

sub_questions.solution:
67, Mist Apartments,
Gagan Vihar, Akash Nagar

11 June 2026

The Editor
The Daily Times
Akash Nagar

Subject: Severe threat posed by open manholes and drains

Sir,
Through the columns of your esteemed newspaper, I wish to draw the attention of the civic authorities towards the life-threatening issue of open manholes and drains in our locality.

These uncovered drains have become a severe safety hazard. Recently, there have been several near-misses where children and elderly residents almost fell in. The danger multiplies at night due to poor street lighting and during the monsoon when streets get waterlogged, making the manholes completely invisible.

It is imperative that the municipal authorities take immediate action to cover these manholes with sturdy lids. Regular maintenance checks should also be instituted to prevent future mishaps.

I hope this letter serves as a wake-up call to the concerned officials to prioritize citizen safety.

Yours sincerely,
Sam/Karen

sub_questions.text_english: Write a letter to the RWA suggesting a dedicated space for senior citizens in the community park.

key_points: Sender address: 43 Jai Apartments, Neerbagh.
Subject: Proposal for a dedicated senior citizen space in the park.
Body: Discuss the need for a peaceful gathering space for elderly well-being.
Suggest the shaded corner near the fountain.
Conclusion requesting swift RWA action.

sub_questions.solution:
43 Jai Apartments,
Neerbagh

11 June 2026

The President
Resident Welfare Association (RWA)
Jai Apartments, Neerbagh

Subject: Proposal for a dedicated space for senior citizens in the community park

Respected Sir/Madam,
I am writing to propose the creation of a dedicated gathering space for the senior citizens of our society within the community park. 

Currently, the park is largely occupied by children playing and residents exercising. Our elderly residents often struggle to find a quiet, safe, and comfortable spot to sit, converse, and relax. I suggest designating the shaded corner near the central fountain exclusively for them. Installing a few comfortable, sturdy benches and perhaps a small gazebo would provide them with a much-needed haven to socialize and enjoy nature, which is vital for their mental and emotional well-being.

I earnestly request the RWA committee to consider this humble suggestion and take the necessary steps to make our society more inclusive for its senior members.

Yours sincerely,
Rohan Monga

questions.text_english:
Attempt any one from (a) and (b) given below:

(a) The detailed global millets production data from different countries is depicted in the pie chart given below. Analyze this chart and write an analytical paragraph in about 120 words, by selecting features that support your analysis and suggesting possible reasons for the variation in production by different countries.

For Visually Impaired Candidates only in lieu of Q. No. 5 (a): Raina is to write an analytical paragraph on 'Importance of Tree Plantation'. Using your own ideas and the information given below, write the paragraph in about 120 words. (One of the best activities - make planet - greener, healthier - to develop biodiversity ensure supply of oxygen for coming generations add to natural beauty - NGOs can be involved for plantation drive.)

OR

(b) There are many benefits of healthy eating for adults as well as children. The following charts reflect the same. Based on the information given in the charts, write an analytical paragraph in about 120 words, assessing the importance of healthy eating for adults as well as children.

For the Visually Impaired Candidates only in lieu of Q. No. 5 (b): Based on the given information, write an analytical paragraph in about 120 words, assessing the importance of healthy eating for both adults and children. (Adults: longer life, healthy weight, keeps skin, teeth, eyes healthy, supports muscles, boosts immunity, strengthens bones, helps digestive system, supports healthy pregnancies and breastfeeding. Children: keeps them healthy and strong, strengthens bones, supports muscles, boosts immunity, supports brain development.)
questions.instruction_line_english: Write an analytical paragraph in about 120 words.
questions.image_description: A pie chart showing Global Millet Production Statistics (FAO 2018). India holds 36%, Niger 14%, China mainland 7%, Mali 6%, Nigeria 5%, Sudan 5%, Burkina Faso 4%, Ethiopia 4%, Chad 3%, Russian Federation 2%, Others 14%. Another set of infographics details the benefits of healthy eating for adults and children.

sub_questions.text_english: Write an analytical paragraph on global millets production or the importance of tree plantation.

key_points: India leads with 36%.
Niger is second with 14%.
African nations dominate the remaining shares.
Reasoning: favorable agro-climatic conditions and cultural dietary habits.

sub_questions.solution: The provided pie chart meticulously illustrates the global distribution of millet production as per FAO 2018 data. India emerges as the undisputed leader, commanding a massive 36% of the global output, highlighting the crop's deep integration into Indian agriculture and dietary staples. Niger follows as a distant second, contributing 14%. Notably, the chart is heavily populated by African nations such as Mali (6%), Nigeria (5%), Sudan (5%), Burkina Faso (4%), Ethiopia (4%), and Chad (3%). This widespread cultivation in Africa and South Asia is primarily driven by millets' high resilience to arid and semi-arid climatic conditions, requiring minimal water and inputs compared to other cereals. Ultimately, the data reflects how agro-climatic suitability directly dictates global agricultural output.

sub_questions.text_english: Write an analytical paragraph assessing the importance of healthy eating for adults as well as children based on the provided charts/data.

key_points: Healthy eating supports growth and immunity in children.
In adults, it prevents chronic diseases and promotes longevity.
Common benefits include healthy weight, strong bones, and healthy skin/eyes.

sub_questions.solution: The provided infographics clearly highlight that healthy eating is paramount across all stages of human life, offering distinct yet interconnected benefits for both children and adults. For children, a nutritious diet serves as the foundation for holistic growth. It ensures robust brain development, strong bones, and healthy muscle growth while actively boosting immunity to fend off early-life infections. As individuals transition into adulthood, the focus of healthy eating shifts towards longevity and disease prevention. Proper nutrition in adults significantly lowers the risk of chronic conditions like heart disease, type 2 diabetes, and certain cancers. Furthermore, across both demographics, a balanced diet is crucial for maintaining optimal body weight, ensuring smooth digestive system functions, and keeping skin, teeth, and eyes healthy.

questions.text_english:
(a) We have, at last, achieved our political emancipation. We pledge ourselves to liberate all our people from the continuing bondage of poverty, deprivation, suffering, gender and other discrimination. Never, never, and never again shall it be that this beautiful land will again experience the oppression of one by another. The sun shall never set on so glorious a human achievement. Let freedom reign. God bless Africa! (Nelson Mandela - Long Walk to Freedom)

OR

(b) The expected call came within a few days. Mrs. Pumphrey was distraught. Tricki would eat nothing. Refused even his favourite dishes; and besides he had bouts of vomiting. He spent all his time lying on a rug, panting. Didn't want to go for walks, didn't want to do anything. I had made my plans in advance. The only way was to get Tricki out of the house for a period. I suggested that he be hospitalised for about a fortnight to be kept under observation. (A Triumph of Surgery)
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the following extracts and answer the questions for any one of the given two, (a) or (b)
questions.solution: Literature extracts are evaluated in sub_questions.
questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela / A Triumph of Surgery

sub_questions.text_english: State any one inference about Nelson Mandela from the given context: We have, at last, achieved our political emancipation.

key_points: He is a visionary leader dedicated to freeing his people.

sub_questions.solution: One inference is that Nelson Mandela has endured a long, arduous struggle for freedom, and he is a resolute leader deeply committed to the liberation and political rights of the South African people.

sub_questions.text_english: State True or False: When Mandela says, God bless Africa, he intends to mean well-being and welfare of only black people in South Africa.
sub_questions.solution: This statement is False. When Mandela says God bless Africa, he is expressing his desire for the well-being and welfare of all its citizens, irrespective of color, having just stated the land will never again experience the oppression of one by another.

sub_questions.text_english: Nelson Mandela's speech is full of optimism. Elaborate in about 40 words with reference to the extract.

key_points: He envisions a future free from all oppression.
He pledges to end poverty and discrimination.

sub_questions.solution: Mandela's speech radiates intense optimism as he confidently pledges to eradicate poverty and all forms of discrimination. His absolute conviction that the land will never, never, and never again face oppression highlights his profound hope for a bright, free future.

sub_questions.text_english: Which phrase would correctly substitute 'so glorious', in the given sentence from the extract. The sun shall never set on so glorious a human achievement.

key_points: so magnificent / such a magnificent

sub_questions.solution: A fitting substitution for 'so glorious' in this context would be 'such a magnificent' or 'so splendid', as they convey the same sense of triumph and grandeur.

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following is not a reason why Mr. Herriot thinks Tricki needs to be taken out of the house for a period?

options_english.A: He wanted to keep Tricki away from Mrs. Pumphrey.
options_english.B: He wanted to keep Tricki under observation.
options_english.C: He wanted to do an experiment on Tricki.
options_english.D: He wanted to improve Tricki's health.

sub_questions.solution: The correct option is C because Mr. Herriot was a responsible veterinary surgeon acting to save the dog's life; he had absolutely no intention of performing experiments on Tricki.

sub_questions.text_english: What was the main reason for Mrs. Pumphrey to be distraught? Answer in about 40 words.

key_points: Tricki stopped eating entirely, even his favorites.
He was vomiting, lethargic, and refused to walk.

sub_questions.solution: Mrs. Pumphrey was severely distraught because her beloved pet, Tricki, had completely stopped eating, even refusing his favorite dishes. Furthermore, he was suffering from bouts of vomiting and spent all his time lying down, panting, and refusing to go for walks.

sub_questions.text_english: State True or False: When Mr. Herriot says, I had made my plans in advance what he actually means is, he had already seen this trauma coming for Tricki.
sub_questions.solution: This statement is True. Mr. Herriot had observed Mrs. Pumphrey's severe overfeeding of Tricki previously and knew that an extreme health crisis was inevitable.

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following best describes Mrs. Pumphrey?
sub_questions.solution: Mrs. Pumphrey is best described as impractical but compassionate. Her immense love for Tricki drives her to overfeed him dangerously, showing her deep compassion but highlighting her lack of practical sense regarding a dog's real dietary needs.

questions.text_english:
(a) In a world of possessions. People will take 
 Balls, balls will be lost always, little boy. 
 And no one buys a ball back. Money is external. 
 He is learning, well behind his desperate eyes, 
 The epistemology of loss, how to stand up 
 Knowing what every man must one day know 
 And most know many days, how to stand up. 
 (The Ball Poem)

OR

(b) Don't eat that chocolate, Amanda! 
 Remember your acne, Amanda! 
 Will you please look at me when I'm speaking to you, Amanda! 
 (I am Rapunzel, I have not a care; 
 life in a tower is tranquil and rare;) 
 (Amanda)

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blank with one word. When the speaker says People will take balls, Balls will be lost always, little boy, his tone is _______
sub_questions.solution: The speaker's tone is philosophical (or practical/realistic). The complete sentence is: When the speaker says People will take balls, Balls will be lost always, little boy, his tone is philosophical.

sub_questions.text_english: The poet says that money is external. What inference can be drawn from this statement? Answer in about 40 words.

key_points: Money can only buy material things.
It cannot buy back the memories or emotional attachment associated with the lost ball.

sub_questions.solution: By stating that money is external, the poet infers that while wealth can easily purchase a new physical ball, it is entirely incapable of buying back the deep emotional attachment, innocence, and precious memories connected to the specific lost possession.

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following best describes the speaker's attitude towards material possessions?
sub_questions.solution: The speaker's attitude is relatively indifferent. By stating that balls will be lost always and money is external, he demonstrates a detached, practical realization that material possessions are ultimately temporary and superficial.

sub_questions.text_english: Identify the poetic device used in And no one buys a ball back.

key_points: Alliteration

sub_questions.solution: The poetic device used here is alliteration, as seen in the repetition of the consonant 'b' sound in the words buys, ball, and back.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the central idea of the poem as reflected in the lines above? Answer in about 40 words.

key_points: The constant nagging and restrictions imposed by parents.
The child's desire for freedom and escapism into a fantasy world.

sub_questions.solution: The central idea reflected here is the sharp contrast between a parent's constant, suffocating nagging about appearances and behavior, and the child's desperate yearning for profound peace, freedom, and escapism, imagined through the tranquil, solitary life of Rapunzel.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence with the appropriate option. Will you please look at me when I'm speaking to you, Amanda! tells us that the mother's attitude is _______
sub_questions.solution: The mother's tone is clearly authoritative. The demand for direct eye contact combined with an exclamation mark shows a strict, commanding approach attempting to force compliance from the child.

sub_questions.text_english: Identify any one poetic device used in the above extract.

key_points: Allusion or Epiphora (Repetition of Amanda)

sub_questions.solution: One prominent poetic device used in the extract is Allusion. The poet references Rapunzel, a well-known fairy tale character, to vividly illustrate Amanda's deep desire to live in isolation and absolute tranquility.

sub_questions.text_english: For what reason does Amanda imagine herself to be Rapunzel?

key_points: To escape her mother's nagging and live peacefully in a tower.

sub_questions.solution: Amanda desperately imagines herself as Rapunzel because she wishes to live completely alone in a high, tranquil tower, entirely free from her mother's relentless nagging and restrictive instructions.

sub_questions.text_english: 'The Tale of Custard the Dragon' is a humorous ballad. How does Ogden Nash create humour and entertainment in the poem ?

key_points: Contrast between appearance and reality.
Use of made-up rhyming words like 'realio, trulio'.

sub_questions.solution: Ogden Nash creates brilliant humor through situational irony and sharp contrast. While the seemingly brave pets cowardly flee from a pirate, the supposedly cowardly dragon Custard bravely eats him. Nash’s playful use of coined words like 'realio' and 'trulio' further enhances the poem's comedic entertainment.

sub_questions.text_english: Justify the title of the play 'The Proposal' with reference to the characters and plot.

key_points: The entire plot revolves around Lomov's intention to propose to Natalya.
The comedy arises from how they keep arguing instead of completing the proposal.

sub_questions.solution: The title 'The Proposal' is highly justified as the entire plot strictly revolves around Lomov’s singular intention to propose marriage to Natalya. The profound comedy and central conflict arise entirely from their absurd inability to stop arguing long enough for the actual proposal to take place.

sub_questions.text_english: The author says - 'During our childhood in Goa, the baker used to be our friend, companion and guide.' Elaborate. (Glimpses of India)

key_points: The baker visited twice a day and was a familiar figure.
Children eagerly awaited his arrival for bread bangles, showing a bond of affection.

sub_questions.solution: The author cherishes the traditional Goan baker (pader) not just as a vendor, but as an intimate part of childhood. The baker visited twice daily, greeting everyone warmly. Children excitedly ran to him for sweet bread bangles, demonstrating a deep, joyous bond of friendship and companionship.

sub_questions.text_english: Do you think you can love a person for his/her inner beauty alone and not care about the physical appearance? Justify with reference to the theme of the poem 'For Anne Gregory'.

key_points: Human love is often heavily influenced by physical appearance.
The poem suggests only God can love someone purely for their inner self.

sub_questions.solution: The poem realistically highlights that humans are inherently drawn to physical appearances, making it incredibly difficult to love someone exclusively for their inner beauty. The poet emphatically concludes that only God possesses the divine capacity to love Anne solely for herself, disregarding her beautiful yellow hair.

Answer any one of the following two questions in 100-120 words:
(a) You have been asked to present an evaluation of the approaches of both, the Baby Seagull and the Pilot who was lost in the clouds, towards achieving their dreams of conquering the skies. Write this presentation draft including your insights, comparing the approaches of both. (Reference: Two Stories About Flying)
OR
(b) You have been chosen to address the school assembly, to speak on the epistemology of loss and the resilience of the human spirit during times of crisis. Prepare the speech draft, with reference to the commonality of themes in The Ball Poem' by John Berryman and From the Diary of Anne Frank'.
questions.chapter: Two Stories About Flying / The Ball Poem & Anne Frank

sub_questions.text_english: Present an evaluation of the approaches of both the Baby Seagull and the Pilot towards achieving their dreams of conquering the skies.

key_points: The Seagull hesitated out of intense fear and lack of confidence.
He needed external motivation (hunger) to take the plunge.
The Pilot was overconfident and driven by a desperate desire to reach home.
He plunged into the storm blindly, risking his life.

sub_questions.solution:
One acknowledges that both the Seagull and the Pilot wanted to conquer the skies; however, their initial approaches and psychological barriers were starkly different. The young seagull was completely paralyzed by an overwhelming fear of failure. He severely lacked self-belief and required an extreme external trigger—intense hunger and his mother's clever trick—to finally plunge into the abyss, ultimately discovering his innate ability to fly.

Conversely, the Dakota pilot was driven by an intense, emotional desire to reach his family for an English breakfast. Instead of fear, he exhibited reckless courage and sheer overconfidence. He deliberately plunged his plane straight into the ominous black storm clouds, totally disregarding his own safety. While the seagull needed to forcefully overcome his crippling cowardice to embrace freedom, the pilot had to miraculously survive his own impulsive bravery. Both ultimately conquered the skies, but their emotional journeys went from opposite ends of the spectrum.

sub_questions.text_english: Prepare a speech draft on the epistemology of loss and resilience, referencing 'The Ball Poem' and 'From the Diary of Anne Frank'.

key_points: Address the school assembly appropriately.
Discuss how 'The Ball Poem' teaches the inevitability of loss and standing back up.
Connect to Anne Frank's diary, representing monumental loss yet incredible resilience.
Conclude on the strength of the human spirit.

sub_questions.solution:
Good morning everyone. Today, I'd like to discuss two pieces of literature that offer a powerful insight into how to deal with loss and the resilience of the human spirit required during times of crisis. 

In John Berryman's 'The Ball Poem', a young boy loses his beloved ball, plunging him into grief. Through this seemingly small event, he learns the profound 'epistemology of loss'—the harsh reality that precious things will be lost, and one must invariably learn to stand up and move forward. This deeply mirrors the monumental, catastrophic loss detailed in 'From the Diary of Anne Frank'. Stripped of her freedom, home, and normal childhood, Anne faces a horrific crisis. Yet, her diary is a shining testament to unyielding human resilience. Instead of completely surrendering to despair, she intensely channeled her thoughts into her writing, maintaining hope and sanity in the darkest annex. 

To conclude, I'd like to say that whether it is the loss of innocence or the loss of freedom, the human spirit's capacity to stand back up remains our greatest strength. Thank you.

sub_questions.text_english: Write a diary entry as Bholi, exploring the themes of 'Girl Child' and 'Impact of Education'.

key_points: Format: Date, Salutation.
Reflect on being a neglected, stuttering girl child treated as a burden.
Describe how the teacher's kindness and education transformed her.
End with her brave decision to reject the greedy Bishamber.

sub_questions.solution:
11 June 2026
Dear Diary,

Today, I look back at my life, and I can hardly recognize the frightened, stuttering girl I once was. For years, being a girl child in my home simply meant being an unwanted burden. With my pockmarks and lack of sense, I was mercilessly mocked and utterly neglected. My parents solely worried about my marriage, treating me like a dumb cow.

However, everything changed the magical day I was forced into a classroom. Education was the beautiful light that completely shattered my darkness. My dear teacher’s gentle encouragement patiently replaced my terrible stutter with a confident, clear voice. Education gave me something a dowry never could: profound self-respect. When Bishamber shamelessly demanded money to marry my scarred face, I did not cry. I boldly threw the garland into the fire. I am no longer a helpless girl; I am Sulekha, an educated, empowered woman ready to support my parents and teach in the very school that saved me.

Sulekha

sub_questions.text_english: Trace the character arc of Griffin in H.G. Wells' Footprints without Feet'.

key_points: Griffin starts as a brilliant scientist who discovers invisibility.
His lawless nature takes over; he burns down a house out of revenge.
He descends into complete criminality, stealing and attacking innocent people.
The arc shows a fall from a genius to a paranoid, lonely menace.

sub_questions.solution:
Griffin’s character arc is a tragic, steep descent from a brilliant scientific mind to a completely unhinged, lawless menace. Initially, he is introduced as an incredibly gifted scientist who successfully achieves the miraculous feat of making the human body entirely transparent. However, his profound lack of morality instantly corrupts his monumental achievement.

Rather than using his brilliant discovery for the greater benefit of humanity, his arc immediately spirals downwards into selfishness and revenge. He maliciously burns down his landlord's house and becomes a homeless wanderer. As he faces the freezing winter, his actions grow increasingly criminal. He brazenly robs a London store, viciously attacks a theatrical shop owner, and terrifies the innocent villagers of Iping, ultimately assaulting a police constable. His character tragically transforms from a celebrated genius into a deeply paranoid, isolated, and utterly sociopathic criminal whose unchecked brilliance becomes a curse to society.
